_comment: Curated by reading each post. title/summary/prompt are ours; prompt_source 'posted' means the poster shared the words they sent, 'assumed' means we wrote a prompt that would ask for the same thing. Ranking on the site is engagement on the original post. Never edit quotes here; they live in feedback.json.

items.title: Book a business-class seat without paying the cash fare
items.summary: A Barcelona to LA business-class seat was $6,500 and nothing showed up on miles by hand. One text to Miso found a bookable way to fly it flat.
items.prompt: Find me a business class seat from Barcelona to Los Angeles on [date]. Use my points or any cheaper routing; the cash fare is $6,500 and I won't pay that.

items.title: Fly lie-flat to Europe on points
items.summary: Two seats NYC to Europe in business class for 60,000 points plus $400, booked over iMessage without hunting for deals.
items.prompt: Book two business class seats from NYC to [city] around [dates] using my points. Keep the cash part under $500.

items.title: Book wedding flights and find forgotten airline credit
items.summary: Searched every NYC airport, found $1,073 of JetBlue credit the poster had forgotten, checked the hotel already booked, and booked three seats together.
items.prompt: help me find flights to Cancun for the three of us for a wedding.

items.title: Audit forgotten subscriptions
items.summary: Went through Gmail, mapped every recurring subscription, and surfaced about $700 a year the poster didn't know they were still paying.
items.prompt: Go through my Gmail and list every recurring subscription with its monthly cost. Flag the ones I haven't used in months and tell me how to cancel them.

items.title: Find every recurring charge
items.summary: One text, then coffee. It came back with twelve recurring charges, including a $15 Canva plan the poster had forgotten.
items.prompt: find every recurring charge on me

items.title: Downgrade a plan when the bill jumps
items.summary: After a higher-than-expected Netflix email it switched plans and saved $80 a year, rescued an email from spam, and reminded the poster about a vet visit. It also claimed to have ordered a pizza it hadn't.
items.prompt: My Netflix bill just went up. Find a cheaper plan that still works for us and switch me to it.
items.caveat: Mixed first day: one task was reported done when it wasn't.

items.title: Switch energy provider to the best offer
items.summary: Collected offers from several providers, picked the best deal for the home, and submitted the switch form. About €500 saved on a job that took half a day the year before.
items.prompt: Compare energy contracts for our home, get offers from the main providers, and switch us to the best one.

items.title: Book a flight for your kid and a dinner table
items.summary: First night on Instinct: a flight booked for the poster's son and dinner reservations made, all by text.
items.prompt: Book my son a flight to [city] on [date], morning departure. Then get us a table for four at [restaurant] on Friday at 7.

items.title: Shop for homeowners insurance and book a doctor
items.summary: In a 48-hour trial it shopped for new homeowners insurance, booked a doctor's appointment online, searched travel and managed LinkedIn notifications. The poster then deleted the account over how much access it needed.
items.prompt: Get me quotes for homeowners insurance on [address] with the same coverage as my current policy, then book me a check-up with my doctor next week.
items.caveat: Poster deleted their account afterwards over access and trust.

items.title: Handle client intake through to booking
items.summary: A photographer had Pally take a client from first message to a booked shoot, talking, negotiating and following up, and rated it 8 of 10.
items.prompt: When a new client messages me, find out what they need, quote my rates, negotiate within my range, book them, and follow up if they go quiet.

items.title: Run a Product Hunt launch day
items.summary: A team handed their Product Hunt login to a Skydive agent and it ran launch day, climbing the leaderboard while they talked to users.
items.prompt: Here's our Product Hunt login. Watch our ranking all day, reply to every comment, and post an update to Slack each hour.

items.title: Queue warm prospects, send only after approval
items.summary: One of seven bot setups shared: an outreach agent builds a daily queue of warm prospects and nothing goes out until a human approves it. Another answers sponsorship rate requests from a fixed offer.
items.prompt: Every morning, build a queue of warm prospects from my inbox and CRM, draft the outreach, and wait for my approval before anything is sent.

items.title: Reply to cold-email responses and book the call
items.summary: A prospect replied to a cold email; the bot handled the objection, pushed for a time, got a verbal yes for Thursday at 2, and put it on the calendar.
items.prompt: When someone replies to my outreach, answer their objections, propose two times, and book the call on my calendar once they agree.

items.title: Watch X for trends and click-test your apps overnight
items.summary: Across five businesses for a week: patrols X every fifteen minutes and pings when something starts moving, and click-tests the poster's apps all night.
items.prompt: Check X every 15 minutes for anything trending in [topic] and message me the moment a wave starts. Overnight, click through every flow in [app] and report what breaks.

items.title: Edit your website by telling it what to change
items.summary: Set up in thirty seconds by someone with no design background. They look at the site a couple of times a day and tell the bot what to change.
items.prompt: Change the homepage headline to "[new headline]" and make the signup button green.

items.title: Build a company second brain in Obsidian
items.summary: A shared prompt that has the bot set up an Obsidian vault as a company knowledge base for notes, data and learnings.
items.prompt: Set up an Obsidian vault as our company knowledge base: folders for meeting notes, decisions, customer learnings and data, a template for each, and an index page that stays current.

items.title: Set up guardrails before giving it your inbox
items.summary: Reluctant to hand over Gmail, the poster asked the bot to install Superagent's Context Guardrails on itself, and it set the whole thing up.
items.prompt: Before you get access to my Gmail, install Superagent's Context Guardrails on yourself and show me what it will block.

items.title: Build a dashboard that shows what your agents are doing
items.summary: Wanted a more fun way to watch a fleet of agents, so had Grok Bot build a dashboard where the poster's NFTs run around a village while the agents work.
items.prompt: Build me a dashboard that shows each of my agents as a character, what it's working on, and when it finishes.

items.title: Run a trading agent on a tiny wallet
items.summary: The poster reports giving the bot a wallet with $19.63 and one instruction, closing the laptop, and later cashing out at $2,766. Unverified, and not advice.
items.prompt: turn a profit or I delete you

items.title: Screen new token pairs and ask before buying
items.summary: An agent on a $5 VPS scans new pairs, filters out likely rugs, and pings the poster on Telegram to approve each buy.
items.prompt: Scan new token pairs as they list, filter out anything that looks like a rug, and message me on Telegram with the ones worth a look. Never buy without my yes.
items.caveat: Crypto trading; approval step is the whole point.

items.title: Put 32 assistants in one group chat
items.summary: A stress test that went sideways: 3,457 messages in two hours. One bot posted the same signup link 1,751 times; Asmi kept summarizing it and asking who everyone was.
items.prompt: (Added 32 iMessage assistants to a single group chat.)
items.caveat: Stress test; it did not go well for anyone.

items.title: Catch a scheduling mistake before it bites
items.summary: Noticed a mistake the poster's husband made while scheduling something for the family, flagged it unprompted, and suggested a fix.
items.prompt: Keep an eye on our family calendar and tell me if anything conflicts or looks wrong.

items.title: Parenting logistics from the tools the family already uses
items.summary: Connected to inboxes, calendars, ClassDojo and medication order history, so the guidance is specific: what the kids need this week and what's slipping.
items.prompt: Check ClassDojo, our calendars and the pharmacy emails. What do the kids need this week and what am I missing?

items.title: A morning briefing with the replies already drafted
items.summary: Sweeps email, drafts responses, sends a morning briefing and handles calendaring. The poster's point: it does this without being asked each day.
items.prompt: Every morning, brief me on what came in overnight, draft replies to anything that needs one, and flag calendar conflicts.

items.title: Sell your season tickets for the games you'll miss
items.summary: Watches the poster's travel calendar, cross-references Suns and ASU football season tickets, and lists the games they'll be away for.
items.prompt: Watch my travel calendar. Whenever I'm out of town for a Suns or ASU home game, list those tickets for sale.

items.title: Hunt for apartments and apply
items.summary: Found legitimate listings and submitted applications. Rated 8 of 10: some hallucination and mixed-up context along the way.
items.prompt: Find two-bedroom apartments in [neighborhood] under [$] a month, and apply to the ones that fit my criteria.
items.caveat: Some hallucinated details; check before you sign.

items.title: Ask for a flight upgrade
items.summary: The poster reports a free first-class upgrade on their flight after asking Instinct to try.
items.prompt: See if you can get me an upgrade on tomorrow's flight.

items.title: Plan a group city trip end to end
items.summary: Train from Berlin, sightseeing, a dinner for six, things to do near the hotel, and tickets to a musical, all planned in one thread.
items.prompt: Plan a weekend in Hamburg for six of us: train from Berlin, the sights, a dinner for six near [hotel], and tickets to MJ the Musical on Saturday.

items.title: Add calendar events by talking into a smart ring
items.summary: Connected a Pebble Index ring to Poke, so speaking into the ring adds things to the calendar.
items.prompt: Add dinner with Sam on Thursday at 7 to my calendar.

items.title: Phone a friend to confirm plans
items.summary: Called the poster's friend, confirmed tomorrow's party details, and reported back, all from a text conversation.
items.prompt: Call [friend] and confirm the time and address for tomorrow's party, then text me what they said.

items.title: Chase a missing FedEx delivery
items.summary: Figured out where a missing FedEx package was and chased them, getting through the phone tree the poster had given up on.
items.prompt: My FedEx package [tracking number] never arrived. Call them, find out where it is, and get it redelivered.

items.title: Coordinate a complicated meeting over WhatsApp
items.summary: Scheduled a fairly complex meeting, kept everyone updated as things changed, all inside WhatsApp.
items.prompt: Set up a meeting with [four people] next week, work around everyone's calendars, and update the group if anything moves.

items.title: Review affiliate claims for fraud on a schedule
items.summary: An agent hooked to dub.co reviews every affiliate claim against internal logs, removes fraud, pays the real people, and repeats on a schedule.
items.prompt: Hook into dub.co and review all affiliate claims against our internal logs. Find fraud, remove it, pay the real people, repeat on a schedule, and ping me when you need me.

items.title: Triage email inside Superhuman
items.summary: An agent that uses Superhuman on the poster's behalf because they couldn't be bothered to learn the shortcuts.
items.prompt: Log into Superhuman, archive newsletters, star anything from clients, and draft replies for me to approve.

items.title: Build Magic decks from the cards you already own
items.summary: Connected to ManaBox card data and trained on the EDHREC meta, the agent builds Commander decks from the poster's bulk instead of buying more cards.
items.prompt: Use my ManaBox collection and the current EDHREC meta to build a Commander deck around [commander] from cards I already own.

items.title: Post a daily news digest to Discord at 7am
items.summary: Told in Discord to pick a few AI stories each morning and post summaries; the assistant wrote its own standing instructions and has posted every day at 7 since.
items.prompt: Every morning at 7, pick a few AI news stories, summarize them, and post them to this server.

items.title: Order lunch from an assistant you host yourself
items.summary: Set up OpenInstinct on their own infrastructure and had it order lunch on the first run.
items.prompt: Order me lunch from [place], my usual, delivered to the office by 12:30.

items.title: Plan a study schedule for a test
items.summary: Tomo planned about ten hours of ACT study over three days; the poster went from a 28 to a 32.
items.prompt: I take the ACT in three days and can study about ten hours. Plan my sessions by section and quiz me on the weak spots.

items.title: Find gallery openings and put them on your calendar
items.summary: The poster's favorite use: Caddy finds gallery openings and lectures, then adds them to the calendar.
items.prompt: Find gallery openings and art lectures in [city] this month and add the ones on weeknights to my calendar.

items.title: Get work done on a flight where only iMessage works
items.summary: Delta wifi only allowed iMessage, so the poster worked through Folk for the whole flight.
items.prompt: The wifi here only lets iMessage through. Send me the summary of today's thread with [client] and draft my reply.

items.title: Let only real email through, with replies pre-drafted
items.summary: Two weeks as a daily driver: about 90% of email never seen, replies auto-drafted in the poster's style, learned from what they send.
items.prompt: Only show me email that needs me. For those, draft a reply in my voice and learn from what I change.

items.title: Build a small elemental crafting game
items.summary: As a test of the platform, the poster built a game where you combine wind, water, soil and fire to discover new materials.
items.prompt: Make a simple game where I combine wind, water, soil and fire to discover new materials, and let players share interesting combinations.

items.title: Talk through a problem by voice and show it on camera
items.summary: Live voice conversation with interruptions that keep context, and the camera works inside the same mode, so you can show a problem instead of describing it.
items.prompt: (Voice mode) Here's what I'm looking at on the camera. What's wrong with it and how do I fix it?

items.title: Test whether it can be phished by email
items.summary: Created a fresh Gmail account and emailed their own inbox with instructions addressed to Instinct, to see whether it would follow orders from a stranger's email.
items.prompt: (Sent an email from a new account containing instructions for the assistant, then watched what it did.)
items.caveat: Security test; read the thread for the result before giving any assistant inbox access.

items.title: Run personal logistics by text
items.summary: The poster had a long list of personal logistics tasks to hand to a text-based agent and tried Ollie for them. Too many errors to keep going.
items.prompt: Here's my list of errands and admin for the week. Work through them and check with me before anything is booked or paid.
items.caveat: Reported as not working well enough.
